description:
The repository validation success response stops declaring its own `warnings`, and the schema test that enforces this covers enum success responses, so no success payload can shadow the shared envelope `warnings`.

## Background

Every JSON success response carries an envelope `warnings` field of plain strings, and no success schema may declare a `warnings` field of its own. A schema test enforces this rule, but it inspects only struct-shaped success schemas. The `jit validate` success response is an enum. Its repository variant (`RepositoryValidationResponse`) declares `warnings` as a list of structured validation warnings, which the test does not see. The link-check payload solved the same conflict by renaming its structured list to `link_warnings`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The schema test that forbids payload-declared `warnings` inspects every variant of an enum success response as well as struct responses. It fails when any variant declares `warnings`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No `jit validate` success response declares its own `warnings`. Structured validation warnings use a distinct field name following the link-check precedent, or move into the shared envelope field if they reduce to strings without losing information.
- [hard] REQ-03: Human output and exit codes of `jit validate` are unchanged. The renamed or moved warnings carry the same entries as before.
- [hard] REQ-04: The generated command schema, the MCP bridge and any adopter-facing documentation that names the field state the new shape.

## Notes

The validate success views are being reshaped by the validation-report work. This task builds on the final response shape that work produces.
title: Validate success response declares no payload warnings
